newsitem.title: USA: USDA crop insurers meet Thursday on 1997 coverage.
newsitem.headline: USDA crop insurers meet Thursday on 1997 coverage.

text.p: Directors of the U.S. Federal Crop Insurance Corp were scheduled to meet Thursday to consider farm income assurance issues, a spokesman said.
The meeting was expected to include discussion of Crop Revenue Coverage, a program that protects farmers against losses caused by low prices or poor yields.

Acceptance Insurance Cos Inc, of Omaha, Neb., said Wednesday that it had FCIC approval to expand Crop Revenue Coverage for 1997 corn and soybeans to 11 more states. The agreement was expected to be raised during the board meeting, which would be held by teleconference.
The FCIC spokesman said there appeared to be agreement on the expansion but the board's opinion was needed.
Senator Pat Roberts, Kansas Republican, said an expansion of CRC would be an important step toward giving farmers risk management tools to go along with the "Freedom to Farm" law.
"I think it's a real step forward," he said of the company's announcement of FCIC approval.

Senate Agriculture Committee chairman Richard Lugar had no immediate comment. The Indiana Republican has expressed concern that CRC be designed to avoid saddling the government with heavy costs for crop protection.
